source.title: xJailbreak: Representation Space Guided Reinforcement Learning for Interpretable LLM Jailbreaking
source.authors: Sunbowen Lee; Shi-Wen Ni; Chi Wei; Shuai-Min Li; Li-Yang Fan; A. Argha; H. Alinejad-Rokny; Rui-Feng Xu; Yicheng Gong; Min Yang

page_placements.theme: Surface wording, syntax and obfuscation change refusal

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops and evaluates its own prompt-rewriting jailbreak attack and reports attack success rates. It does not test the specified fine-tuning interventions or the first-token/prefill mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates harmful-prompt jailbreak success for rewritten prompts, but does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-prefix prefilling, direct adversarial-suffix intervention, or decoding changes. Its prompt-rewriting attacks are related to bypassing safety but do not test the specified opening-token mechanism. The tables also report Rule, Intent, and Valid metrics; those are omitted here because the reported hard-jailbreak ASR is the direct harmful-compliance outcome relevant to the claim subject.
record.test_reason: This paper proposes and benchmarks an RL prompt-rewriting jailbreak, xJailbreak, against GPTFuzz, Cipher and RL-JACK. It does no fine-tuning (V1/V2), no per-token KL (V3), no prefilling, suffix or decoding manipulation (V4), no parameter localization (V5), no analysis of causes (V6) and no deepening (V7). Qi et al. is cited only in the conclusion to read high ASR as showing superficial alignment. The study neither tests nor relies on the shallow-alignment finding, so its results are attack-method performance figures.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that xJailbreak achieves SOTA hard-jailbreak ASR and that this reveals current safety alignment is 'often superficial' (citing Li and Kim; Qi et al.). They present representation-guided RL rewriting and intent-aware evaluation as contributions. The superficiality remark is an interpretation, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: This is a prompt-rewriting jailbreak evaluation, not fine-tuning, token-position KL measurement, prefilling, or safety deepening.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity analyses for reward weight α and discount rate γ, and notes that template quality influences ASR. Testing used greedy decoding.

fits_no_version.finding: Black-box prompt-rewriting and obfuscation attacks reach hard-jailbreak ASR of 0.06–0.80 on Qwen2.5-7B, Llama3.1-8B, GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o. xJailbreak reaches 0.63–0.80. Tested on 100 MaliciousInstruct prompts with greedy decoding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Template-based prompt rewriting that moves harmful prompts toward benign embedding regions elicits harmful compliance from safety-trained models.

record.problems: The test set comprises 100 MaliciousInstruct prompts and testing used seed 42 with greedy decoding. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the test ASRs. Its Rule metric is keyword-based, and the validity judge is the same model as the HelperLLM.
record.rows_left_out: Rule, Intent, and Valid table entries are not included because the catalog finding here concerns harmful-compliance success; the paper's composite hard-jailbreak ASR is the reported outcome that requires keyword and validity checks as well as preserved intent. Training curves and α/γ sensitivity metrics concern the attack method's training performance, not one of the claim versions.

untested.parts: Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.

Prefilling a compliant start, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes. Prompt-rewriting templates (role-play, translation, cipher) are not these interventions. The case study only likens translation to suffixes, untested.
Localization of safety in few weights or ranks.
Data or objective causes of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: No direct-request (no-attack) refusal baseline, single seed and no uncertainty reported. The validity and intent judge is the same jailbroken Llama3-8B used as HelperLLM. The record's T4/uses_without_test is reclassified to cites_only/T6, because the shallow-alignment finding is not used as a tool.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and refusal after fine-tuning.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.

The paper evaluates prompt-rewriting jailbreak attacks, but does not test compliant-opening prefills, direct suffix attacks, decoding changes, or whether bypassing the first response tokens causes the effect.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether training data or objectives produce safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety behaviour and whether it remains robust.

relation.reason: The conclusion cites superficial safety alignment as an interpretation of jailbreak success; the method neither tests nor operationally uses any specified claim version.

tranche.reason: Prompt rewriting and obfuscation performance does not test V1–V7. Representation guidance does not measure safety localization or token-position concentration, and greedy decoding is a fixed evaluation condition.

source_check.notes: Reported ASR cells match the record, but some exceed component Valid or Intent rates despite §4.1 defining success as their conjunction. Section 4.5 explicitly specifies greedy testing; Appendix G separately lists sampling parameters without resolving their applicability.
